subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw keep default steer as boundary-based same-turn steering, or add an explicit soft-steer mode/command that interrupts or pauses active generation or tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context?
rationale: The choice changes shared runtime semantics, channel UX, Codex app-server integration, transcript/tool pairing, and compatibility with existing steer/followup/interrupt modes.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document the current model-boundary behavior as the supported default and use narrower PRs only to ensure messages reach that existing policy.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change default steer to the stronger lifecycle only after maintainer-approved upgrade proof and channel/runtime compatibility coverage.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history and the prior replacement PR make this the strongest available owner for active-run steering semantics.
